newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex called higher on cold weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex called higher on cold weather.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil was called higher Monday after cold temperatures descended on the northeastern United States this weekend, with crude and gasoline prices expected to follow heat, traders said.
"It's follow through from Friday on the colder temperatures. There are a lot of shorts being suqeezed," said a trader.

Refined products were called 0.50 to 0.75 cent a gallon higher while crude was called 15 to 20 cents a barrel higher. Gasoline traded 2.00 cents up on ACCESS, but dealers said the print was one trader needing to cover a short position.
"It's a total anomaly," said a dealer of the gasoline trade, adding there was no news that would push gasoline higher than heating oil.
Forecasts called for temperatures in the Northeast to be 10 to 14 degress below normal through mid-week.
On Friday, December heating oil settled up 2.04 cents a gallon at 68.93 cents and December gasoline ended up 1.47 cents a gallon at 65.27 cents. December crude closed up 85 cents at $23.59 a barrel.
Chartists pegged resistance for December crude at $24.00 and December heating oil at 70.00 cents.
Resistance for December gasoline was pegged at 66.00 cents.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
